title: Reuse bullet objects in a game
description: BulletPool keeps a fixed set of Bullet objects. fire() acquires a bullet from the pool, marks it active, and returns it. When the bullet hits or expires, recycle() resets it and returns it to the pool. If no bullets are free, fire() returns null (the shot is skipped). Fill in fire() and recycle().
hints: Keep two collections: one for available bullets, one for active bullets
fire() moves a bullet from available to active and sets its active flag
recycle() resets the bullet and moves it back to available
issues: Allocating a new Bullet object on every shot causes frequent garbage collection spikes
Without a cap on active bullets, the game has no way to limit simultaneous projectiles
overallGoal: Use the Object Pool pattern to reuse a fixed set of Bullet objects across many shots, avoiding repeated allocation and enabling a hard cap on simultaneous projectiles.
goals: fire() returns an active Bullet from the pool, or null when the pool is exhausted
recycle() resets the bullet and makes it available for the next fire() call
The total number of Bullet objects never exceeds the pool size
